title: On $\varepsilon$-Matrix Product Factorization of graphs
summary: We introduce an approximate version of matrix product factorization for graphs. A simple graph $G$ on $n$ vertices is said to admit an $\varepsilon$-matrix product factorization if there exist simple graphs $H$ and $K$ on the same vertex set such that $A(H)A(K)$ and $A(G)$ disagree in at most $\varepsilon n^{2}$ entries. This Hamming-type relaxation preserves, outside the error set, the exact interpretation of each edge as having a unique $H$-then-$K$ two-step witness.
